summary: 5. The instant petition was filed on 11.03.2024 and listed for hearing on 19.08.2024. During the course of the hearing held on 19.08.2024, _considering the submissions made by the parties and having observed that the issue involved primarily pertained to terms & conditions of the RfS documents, the Commission issued notice on maintainability as well as merits, subject to just exceptions._ Subsequently, the matter was listed on 14.11.2024 & 28.04.2025. A detailed hearing was held on 07.07.2025. During the hearing held on 07.07.2025, the parties made their submissions. Based on the request of the parties, the Commission permitted both parties to file their notes of arguments/ written submissions, if any, within a week, and the matter was reserved for Orders. _5.5.1 Subsequent to conclusion of the e-RA process, the bidders in the “Green” and “Orange” zones as per Clause 5.4.4(vi) above, will be listed in the increasing order of the tariffs discovered at the end of e-RA._ # **_Re. Jurisdiction of the Commission to entertain the present petition in exercise of power under section 79(1)(b) read with section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003_** - _The Commission may, for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these regulations on its own motion or on an application made before the Commission by any party or interested person._ 14. On the basis of the submissions of the contracting parties, the following issue arises for adjudication: _In case it becomes imperative for the Procurer/intermediate_ **_ procurer to deviate from these Guidelines and/or the SBDs, the same shall be subject to approval by the Appropriate Government before the initiation of bidding process itself. The Appropriate Government shall approve or require modification to the bid documents within a reasonable time not exceeding 60 (sixty) days. _** **_ In the event CERC is the Appropriate Commission, any dispute arises claiming any change in or regarding determination of the tariff or any tariff related matters, or which partly or wholly could result in change in tariff, such dispute shall be adjudicated by the CERC. _** _All other disputes shall be resolved by arbitration Dispute Resolution Committee set up by the Government, failing which by arbitration under the Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. In the event SERC / JERC is the Appropriate Commission, then all disputes shall be adjudicated by the SERC / JERC or shall be referred for arbitration by the SERC / JERC._ _5.5.1 Subsequent to conclusion of the e-RA process, the bidders in the “Green” and “Orange” zones as per Clause 5.4.4(vi) above, will be listed in the increasing order of the tariffs discovered at the end of e-RA._ 22. From the above, we observe that as per the MoP Guidelines dated 09.06.2023, it is stipulated that (i) in case it becomes imperative for the Procurer/intermediate procurer to deviate from these Guidelines and/or the SBDs, the same shall be subject to approval by the Central Government before the initiation of the bidding process itself. The Central Government shall approve or require modification to the bid documents within a reasonable time not exceeding 60 (sixty) days; (ii) Further, in case any difficulty arises in giving effect to any provision of these Guidelines or interpretation of the Guidelines or modification to the Guidelines, the Ministry of Power is empowered to do the same in consultation with the MNRE; (iii) furthermore, this Commission is empowered to adjudicate only in case any dispute arises claiming any change in or regarding determination of the tariff or any tariff related matters, or which partly or wholly could result in change in tariff. All other disputes are to be resolved by arbitration through the Dispute Resolution Committee (DRC) set up by the Government. _(87) It is true that as far as the said case is concerned, the case arose from claims which were made under the PPA on the basis that there were changes in law apart from the argument that a case of Force Majeure was made out._ **_ It is not a case which actually on facts involved the Court dealing with a case arising from the fixation of tariff under Section 63. In fact, it arose after a PPA was approved and the rates were fixed already under Section 63. _** _However, if we notice the contents of para 19 and 20, the principle which the first respondent seeks to canvas before us does not appear to_ _(91) We are of the view that the Tribunal cannot indeed make a new bargain for the parties. The Tribunal cannot rewrite a contract solemnly entered into. It cannot ink a new agreement._ **_ Such residuary powers to act which varies the written contract cannot be located in the power to regulate. _** _The power cannot, at any rate, be exercised in the teeth of express provisions of the contract._ - b) The Hon’ble Supreme Court rejected the argument that, unlike the generality of contracts, a regulated contract, which is a long-term contract or an incomplete contract, generates space for power with the appropriate regulatory body to revisit the rates and thereby vouchsafe a fair deal to both sides, be it a seller or the procurer. 32. We observe that the MoP Guidelines dated 09.06.2023 stipulate that in case of deviation from the Guidelines and/or the SBDs, the same shall be subject to approval by the Central Government before the initiation of the _bidding process itself_ . This Commission is empowered to adjudicate only in case any dispute arises claiming any change in or regarding the determination of the tariff or any tariff-related matters, and all other disputes are to be resolved by arbitration through the Dispute Resolution Committee (DRC) set up by the Government.
